title: From an example to a function
description:
Take the example from `std::regex_search`'s page and turn it into a function you can reuse.

```
find all numbers in "Room 101, floor 3, 42 chairs": 101 3 42
find all words starting with c: chairs
```
hints: `std::sregex_iterator` walks every match; the page shows a loop with it (lesson 5.01).
Making one small change and running it again is the fastest way to learn what each line of an example does.
requirements: Start from the page's example, change one thing at a time, and run it after each change.
End with `std::vector<std::string> findAll(const std::string& text, const std::string& pattern)`.
Keep the original example in a comment with a note on what you changed.
stretch: Return the positions too, as `(position, text)` pairs.
